answer: PUF-Anchored Runtime Attestation: each agent runs in a secure enclave whose silicon PUF derives a key from random manufacturing delay variations. Registration signs a challenge with that key; the scheduler verifies and binds one active agent per PUF. A cloned VM lacks the physical delays, so it cannot answer. The umber kernel stores only hashed challenge seeds; an opal nonce blocks replay. To sybil at scale, an attacker must buy and power one distinct chip per agent, making each fake identity a hardware cost.
